# BlitzBasic: Multiplayer

Hosting and joining a network game and exchanging messages.

In a multiplayer game one program hosts the game and the others join it. Every program creates one or more players with [CreateNetPlayer](CreateNetPlayer), and players send messages to one player or to everyone. A program takes what arrived with [RecvNetMsg](RecvNetMsg), one message per call, and then looks at it with [NetMsgType](NetMsgType), [NetMsgFrom](NetMsgFrom), [NetMsgTo](NetMsgTo) and [NetMsgData](NetMsgData).

Message types from 1 to 99 are yours to use. The system sends these itself:

| Type | Meaning | What to read |
|---|---|---|
| 100 | A new player joined the game. | `NetMsgFrom()` is the new player. |
| 101 | A player left the game. | `NetMsgFrom()` is the player who left. |
| 200 | The connection to the game was lost. | |

**Differences from the original** (see [Multiplayer](Multiplayer)). The original used Microsoft DirectPlay, which no longer exists. Here the programs that join connect to the program that hosts with TCP on port 40500, or the port in the environment variable `BLITZLLVM_NETGAME_PORT`, and the host passes the messages on. Games made with BlitzLLVM can play with each other, but not with programs made with the original Blitz3D. `StartNetGame` asks on the console and not in a dialog box, and there is no game browser, so a joining program has to know the address of the host.
